title: Cool summer holidays in Europe: 10 places that stay under 25°C in August
author: Matt
intro: If you'd rather not swelter, Norway, Iceland, the Faroe Islands, the Baltic capitals, Brittany and the Alps all usually stay under 25°C in August. Here are 10 cooler places, from 13°C to 24°C, and what each is like in summer.
seo_title: Cool summer holidays in Europe: under 25°C in August
seo_description: Iceland and the Faroes are about 13°C in August, Bergen 19°C, Copenhagen and Stockholm 21°C, Brittany 22°C. 10 cool summer holidays compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Coolest:** Iceland and the Faroes, 13°C
- **Cool and scenic:** Norway, 15-19°C
- **Warm, not hot:** Baltic cities, 20-21°C
- **Mountain air:** the Alps, 20-24°C

All the temperatures here are average daytime highs for August, from long-term climate data in our destination guides. Heatwaves do happen, even in the north, so these are typical figures rather than promises.

The coolest places are also the most remote, so the further north you go, the more you'll pay and the more you'll want a car or good walking boots.

sections.heading: The far north: Iceland, the Faroes and Lofoten
sections.text:
At around 13 to 15°C, these are true cool-weather holidays. Pack layers and a waterproof, and expect weather that changes by the hour.

- **[Reykjavik](/destinations/reykjavik)** is the base for the Golden Circle and the south coast waterfalls, and our [Iceland in 4 days](/blog/iceland-in-4-days) post plans a short trip.
- **The [Faroe Islands](/destinations/faroe-islands)** are wilder and emptier, with grass-roofed villages and sea cliffs.
- **[Lofoten](/destinations/lofoten)** has jagged peaks rising straight out of the sea, red fishing cabins and long, light evenings.

Local knowledge: the midnight sun in Lofoten runs from late May to mid-July. By August the sun sets again, but the evenings are still light until late.

sections.heading: Norway's fjords and the Baltic capitals
sections.text:
[Bergen](/destinations/bergen), at about 19°C, is the gateway to the western fjords, with a harbour of wooden houses and a funicular up Mount Fløyen. It's one of Europe's rainiest cities, so bring a raincoat whatever the forecast.

The Nordic and Baltic capitals are warmer, at around 20 to 21°C, which is ideal city break weather. [Copenhagen](/destinations/copenhagen) has clean harbour baths for a swim, [Stockholm](/destinations/stockholm) has thousands of islands to explore by boat, [Helsinki](/destinations/helsinki) has public saunas by the sea, and [Tallinn](/destinations/tallinn) has one of Europe's best-preserved medieval old towns. All are short, direct flights from the UK.

sections.heading: Mountains and the Atlantic coast
sections.text:
- **The Alps:** [Zermatt](/destinations/zermatt), under the Matterhorn, is about 20°C in the village and much cooler higher up. [Interlaken](/destinations/interlaken) and the [Dolomites](/destinations/dolomites) are a little warmer, at about 23 to 24°C, with cool mornings and evenings.
- **Brittany:** [Saint-Malo](/destinations/saint-malo) is about 22°C, with beaches, a walled old town and easy ferries from the south coast of England.
- **Northern Spain:** [Asturias](/destinations/asturias) and [San Sebastián](/destinations/san-sebastian) are greener and cooler than the south, at about 24 to 25°C, though they're on the edge of our 25°C line.

Tip: in the mountains, even on a hot day in the valley, it can be close to freezing at the top of a cable car. Take a warm layer up with you.

sections.heading: Who a cool summer suits
sections.text:
- **Anyone who hates the heat**, or who sleeps badly in hot rooms without air conditioning.
- **Walkers and cyclists**, for whom 15 to 20°C is ideal.
- **Mixed groups**, where one person loves the sun and another can't stand it. Our post on [holidays when everyone wants something different](/blog/when-everyone-wants-a-different-holiday) has more ideas.
- **Summer holiday families** who want to avoid southern Europe's heatwaves.

For hotter options, our [summer holidays](/destinations/summer-holidays) page covers both, and the [where to go in August](/destinations/where-to-go-in-august) page compares the month's choices. If you can't decide between them, add a few to somewhere.party and let the draw pick.

faqs.question: Where in Europe is cool in August?
faqs.answer: Iceland and the Faroe Islands are about 13°C, northern Norway about 15°C, Bergen about 19°C, and Copenhagen, Stockholm and Tallinn about 21°C.

faqs.question: Where can I go on holiday to avoid the heat in summer?
faqs.answer: Head north or up. Scandinavia, Iceland, the Baltic capitals, Brittany and the Alps usually stay under 25°C in July and August.

faqs.question: Is Norway warm in summer?
faqs.answer: Mild rather than warm. Bergen averages about 19°C in August and Lofoten about 15°C, with long, light evenings and some rain.

faqs.question: Is Copenhagen hot in August?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The average high is about 21°C, which is comfortable for cycling and sightseeing, though there are warmer spells.
